review_notes: I read the whole file (lines 1–75). I also searched the UniformKServer directory for how Data.heavyFlag, Data.positive and the Tape type are used. Every declaration is a bridge lemma tied to the concrete structure Data X N H. Each one is specialised to the actual tape ω.1, to D.r, to the constants 3r and 120r, and to the HeavyProcess/HeavyRecords API. The real numbers are the codomain of the metric and of the potential, so a field-class generalisation of the scalar would not be natural. heavyFlag_at is only an unfolding of the heavyFlag definition, and I found no weaker hypothesis that makes it more general. In heavy_stationary and heavy_mover the proof uses ω only through ω.1, but I could not show that a different formulation is more useful to users. I found no justified generalisation that is both useful and avoids new mathematics. I did not open the full definitions of Tape or HeavyProcess.run_stationary_payment, so a generalisation inside those definitions remains unchecked.
